$comment: THE FEATURES THIS PRODUCT HAS, AND HOW EACH ONE IS ACTUALLY TURNED OFF.
This built-in product manifest distinguishes three mechanisms that are often
described as disabled but provide different boundaries:
'disabled', they stop three different attackers, and a settings screen that
blurs them is lying:
absent        The code is not in the payload. Enforced at BUILD time by
tools/check-payload-boundary.mjs, which is fail-closed and
treats an unclassified file as a failure. This is the ONLY
tier that stops a rogue agent, because an agent with a shell
can do anything the shipped code could do.
unregistered  The code is on disk but its tools are never defined, so they
are absent from tools/list and dispatch refuses the id. This
stops an honest mistake, a confused agent, and a prompt
injection reaching for a tool. It does NOT stop an agent that
can spawn a process. Instantly reversible.
gated         The tools exist and the policy kernel refuses without the
entitlement. For anything that must not be forgeable this is
checked SERVER-SIDE by pairId, the way
providers/hosted-relay-entitlement.js already does -- it
never reads anything from the customer's machine.
At the unrestricted permission level, `unregistered` is a blast-radius control and not a
security boundary, and this file says so in the tier field of every entry so
no settings copy can promise more than the mechanism delivers.
WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT. It is not the source of truth for whether a feature is
on. src/lib/capability-features.js resolves that from the RESOLVED TOOL
REGISTRY and the filesystem at the moment it is asked, so the onboarding line
cannot name a feature whose tools are not really there. A confined permission
tier shrinks listTools, and the line shrinks with it. This file declares what
COULD exist and how to look for it; the resolver decides what DOES.
